newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE utility demand slides as illegal workers leave.
newsitem.headline: UAE utility demand slides as illegal workers leave.

text.p: Water and power demand in the United Arab Emirates has fallen 10-15 percent since some 200,000 illegal foreign workers left the country under a government amnesty, a UAE official said in remarks published on Sunday.

"The consumption of water and electricity in the UAE has gone down by 10 to 15 percent following the departure of almost 200,000 amnesty-seekers," the Khaleej Times newspaper said, quoting a Ministry of Water and Electricity official.
"Most of them have abused the generosity of the government and taken full advantage of the facilities in all residential buildings," the unnamed official said.

Diplomats estimate 200,000 illegal workers -- or around 10 percent of the population -- have left the oil-rich state in the past few months to avoid stiff new immigration laws which came into effect on Friday.
Water and electricity is heavily subsidised in the UAE.

The paper quoted Hassan al-Nassay, director general of Water and Electricity Department in Abu Dhabi -- the biggest emirate and the capital -- as saying, "The actual cost of water per 1,000 gallons (4,545 litres) ranges from 28 to 30 dirhams (around $8) which is mostly borne by the government.
In July the department raised water charges to 10 dirhams per 1,000 gallons from seven dirhams.
